summary: Add a separate n8n community-node package that uses only public identity-scoped REST/webhook contracts, plus an additive evidence-preserving webhook subscription disable operation required by workflow lifecycle.

impacts.evidence: n8n is treated as an external authenticated principal. Organization/workspace selectors are absent from credentials/UI and explicitly rejected by the shared query client; TORGNEXA derives scope from identity on every public API call.

Bearer credentials stay in n8n credential storage and webhook receiver secrets stay in workflow static state; management responses do not disclose signing material and node error projection does not return arbitrary server payloads.
OpenAPI is additively bumped to 0.7.0 with idempotent DELETE /webhook-subscriptions/{subscription_id}; generated SDK inventory increases from 29 to 30 operations without changing existing operations.
Task 019 consumes existing canonical webhook event names and permits additive canonical event strings; it changes no event schema, catalog entry or envelope version.
The n8n package calls public REST/webhook surfaces only and does not link to or modify Connector SDK root interfaces, provider manifests, capabilities or connector runtime types.
No migration is required: durable webhook subscriptions already model disabled state. Repository code performs an idempotent state transition using existing columns and retains historical rows.

HTTPS is required except loopback development, redirects are disabled, tenant-selector injection is rejected, raw request bytes are mandatory for HMAC verification, replay is bounded to five minutes and no raw/internal privileged node is exposed.

Task 019 intentionally ships read-only Product/Order operations and no mutation escape hatch. Future sensitive writes must be reviewed public endpoints and continue through Task-017 approval policy rather than n8n internal access.

Webhook lifecycle disable preserves the subscription row, durable delivery history, correlation and replay/DLQ evidence instead of hard-deleting operational history; no domain evidence is synthesized inside n8n.

Subscription disable is idempotent for active/already-disabled rows, and trigger reconfiguration disables the prior subscription before registering a fresh id/secret, preventing intentional duplicate active receivers.

The trigger registers only an externally reachable HTTPS callback through Task-063. Existing SSRF/delivery controls remain authoritative and the new DELETE path revokes delivery signing material while retaining evidence.

n8n activation/deactivation maps to durable subscription state and existing Task-063 delivery attempt/DLQ evidence; the node returns bounded HTTP status/title errors rather than high-cardinality raw server errors.

The REST change is additive and has no schema migration. Package rollback can stop publishing the node while existing disabled/active subscriptions remain manageable through public webhook lifecycle operations.

Go tests cover authenticated-scope disable/idempotent secret revocation; offline TypeScript tests cover URL/query isolation, authenticated transport, canonical event normalization and exact-body signature/replay/tamper behavior; SDK drift is regenerated from OpenAPI.
